title: Bonfire Night With Kids: Firework Displays and Safety
description: Planning Bonfire Night with kids? Why organised firework displays are the safest choice, booking tips, ear defenders for little ones, sparkler safety and pets.
h1: Bonfire Night with kids: firework displays and safety
intro: Bonfire Night falls on Thursday 5 November in 2026, with lots of displays on the weekends either side. Here’s how to enjoy the bangs and sparkles safely, at any age.

image.alt: Twinkling red and white festive lights

cardText: Organised displays, booking, ear defenders and sparkler safety.

blocks.title: Scout’s firework tip
blocks.text: Organised public displays are the safest (and often cheapest) way to see fireworks. Book online early: many sell cheaper advance tickets and some sell out.
points: Ear defenders for babies and toddlers
Gloves on for sparklers, and a bucket of water for used ones
Agree a meeting point in the crowd

sections.html: Councils, schools, sports clubs and attractions run displays around 5 November, often with food stalls and fairground rides. Search your council’s website and local news for listings. Some heritage railways, castles and theme parks run firework events too: see seasonal events.

• Bring ear defenders for babies and toddlers.
  • Stand further back: you still see the sky, but it’s less loud.
  • Early-evening or “quiet” displays suit younger children.

• Sparklers aren’t recommended for under-5s.
  • Wear gloves, hold them at arm’s length and light one at a time.
  • Put used sparklers hot end down in a bucket of water. They stay hot for a long time.
Fireworks can frighten pets. Our sister site has tips on keeping pets calm during fireworks.

faqs.a: Bonfire Night is on Thursday 5 November 2026. Many organised displays take place on the weekends before and after.

faqs.q: What age can children use sparklers?
faqs.a: Sparklers aren’t recommended for under-5s. Older children should wear gloves and always be supervised.
